before: Source classes: cfDNA is DNA outside intact cells in a sample, and ctDNA is the tumour-derived part of that pool, so the two are related materials and not rival tests. In healthy donors a methylation atlas of 25 tissues and cell types attributed plasma cfDNA to white blood cells (55%), erythrocyte progenitors (30%), vascular endothelial cells (10%) and hepatocytes (1%) (Moss 2018). A tumour adds DNA only when it contributes, and the tumour share may be small or absent in the sample drawn even when cancer exists elsewhere.

Scale: plasma DNA fragments show a pattern reminiscent of nuclease-cleaved nucleosomes with a peak at 166 base pairs (Lo 2010, in maternal plasma), and tumour-derived fragments are enriched at 90 to 150 base pairs (Mouliere 2018). One assay input in a breast-cancer comparison was 4,500 amplifiable copies, about 15 nanograms (Santonja 2023), and at about 3.3 picograms per haploid genome copy 1 nanogram is roughly 300 copies (arithmetic from genome size). In a fictional single-locus model with 4,500 amplifiable opportunities and target-allele probability 1 in 100,000, the expected target count is 0.045. The target-allele probability is not automatically a tumour-DNA fraction: copy number, variant multiplicity and clone representation matter.

Yield is not origin: in a fictional experiment equal 1 mL plasma aliquots give 2 and 4 nanograms of cfDNA and no tumour-attributed signal is reported. Total DNA doubled, but tumour fraction and any tumour-DNA fold change cannot be calculated because tumour attribution was not measured. A fragment's source needs evidence such as paired white-blood-cell and tumour sequencing (Razavi 2019), and a variant seen in plasma is not automatically tumour-derived.

Method card: measures selected features of plasma DNA by a stated sequencing or molecular method, from a finite plasma aliquot that testing consumes. Output is detected or not detected, variant fractions, molecule concentrations or model estimates, each with its own unit. It cannot give an all-body cell count, lesion location, viability or treatment benefit, and validity belongs to the exact specimen, assay version and intended use.

Collection conditions can change the mixture before testing: blood-cell breakdown adds genomic DNA and can dilute a tumour fraction. The NCI biospecimen practices document, revised February 2025, prefers plasma to serum. Its protocol recommends EDTA, accepts acid citrate dextrose, and advises avoiding heparin and citrate; the literature-summary section separately reports results with several anticoagulants when processing was immediate. For EDTA blood the protocol prefers centrifugation within 2 hours and accepts up to 4 hours at room temperature or 24 hours at 4 degrees Celsius; it recommends stabilising tubes for anticipated delays over 2 hours. These are recommendations for that specimen workflow, not a universal acceptance rule for every assay. Extraction and library preparation then retain only some available molecules, so the volume drawn is not the volume evaluated.

before: Leading programmes: Ebert (Dana-Farber/Broad) and Jaiswal (Stanford) who defined CHIP; Levine and Bolton (MSK) on therapy-related clonal haematopoiesis.

Clonal haematopoiesis (CH) is the broader phenomenon of blood-cell clones carrying acquired changes. In the 2022 WHO myeloid classification, CHIP requires a somatic mutation in a myeloid-malignancy-associated gene at a variant allele fraction of at least 2%, or at least 4% for X-linked gene mutations in males, without a diagnosed haematological disorder or unexplained cytopenia (Khoury 2022). Persistent unexplained cytopenia changes the classification question. These are criteria for a named category, not a rule that every smaller blood-cell clone is absent, tumour-derived or a sequencing error.

Which genes: in blood-cell exomes from 17,182 people most clonal variants fell in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, were rare before age 40, and were seen in 9.5% of people aged 70 to 79 (Jaiswal 2014). ASXL1 mutations were enriched in current or former smokers, and radiation, platinum and topoisomerase II inhibitors selected for DNA-damage-response genes (TP53, PPM1D, CHEK2), with sequential samples showing those clones outgrowing others after exposure (Bolton 2020). In 8,810 people with non-haematological cancers, PPM1D and TP53 mutations were associated with prior chemotherapy, and clonal haematopoiesis was found in 25% (Coombs 2017).

Source attribution in plasma, interpretation rule: TP53 is a tumour gene and also a therapy-selected blood-cell gene, so a TP53 variant in plasma after chemotherapy can come from either compartment. Matched white-blood-cell DNA and the tumour's variant list, where available, help assess its origin; some variants remain ambiguous. In Razavi's paired sequencing 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 controls without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, and variants that could not be separated from white-blood-cell DNA kept an explicit ambiguous category, so subtracting every blood match is not a complete attribution method.

Fictional example: a plasma assay detects a variant that sensitive matched blood-cell sequencing finds at 0.8% VAF. The blood result supports a blood-cell contribution even below the 2% cut-off, but it does not make the variant CHIP or exclude a tumour contribution, because tumour evidence, shared variants and each method's limits still apply. Matched sequencing has its own gene coverage, depth and detection rules, so a clone below its sensitivity can stay unseen, and a clone finding is not a leukaemia diagnosis or a solid-tumour treatment instruction.

Reading the figures: a variant allele fraction counts variant alleles among the alleles evaluated and is not automatically the percentage of cells. Acquired (somatic) means not inherited and does not mean malignant. There is no age at which a plasma variant can simply be dismissed. Sequential samples show clones with DNA-damage-response mutations outgrowing others after radiation, platinum or topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure (Bolton 2020), which is selection of clones that can already be present and does not mean every new detection was caused by treatment.

Prostate cancer: this is where clonal haematopoiesis does concrete harm. In 69 men with advanced prostate cancer, clonal haematopoiesis variants at 2% or more were present in plasma from 13, 19%, and 7, 10%, had one in a gene used to decide PARP inhibitor candidacy, most often ATM, accounting for almost half of all somatic DNA repair variants detected. A paired whole-blood control distinguishes them (Jensen 2021).

before: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. One established epithelial method captures with EpCAM, then checks cell shape, a nucleus, cytokeratin and absence of CD45, which is one operational definition and not a universal rule for all circulating tumour cells or tumour types. Physical methods select by size or deformability and remove or retain different cells, so marker independence is not unbiased recovery. A negative capture, such as zero qualifying cells in 7.5 mL, does not show that no tumour cells circulate and does not predict a ctDNA result, because free DNA fragments are a separate analyte.

Scale and scope: in the CellSearch system, 1 of 344 healthy or non-malignant-disease subjects (0.3%) had two or more cells per 7.5 mL, against 36% of 2,183 samples from 964 people with metastatic carcinoma, with detection of two or more cells in 57% of prostate, 37% of breast, 30% of colorectal and 20% of lung cancer samples (Allard 2004). Spiked-cell recovery averaged at least 85% over 5 to 1,142 cells. These describe that device and population.

Prognosis is not utility: in a prospective study of 177 people with metastatic breast cancer, a baseline count of 5 or more per 7.5 mL in the training set went with a median progression-free survival of 2.7 months against 7.0 (Cristofanilli 2004). In SWOG S0500, of 595 evaluable patients 123 with persistently raised counts were randomised to continue or change chemotherapy, and median overall survival was 10.7 and 12.5 months (P = .98), so that early-switch strategy did not extend survival (Smerage 2014). That bounds one strategy and neither validates nor excludes other uses of the count.

Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) describes changes in cell state and marker expression. Yu and colleagues reported epithelial and mesenchymal changes in circulating breast tumour cells and associations with progression (2013). As a measurement inference, enrichment requiring an epithelial marker can under-represent cells with little of that marker; physical capture has different selection effects. Neither route is a census of all circulating tumour cells. The study does not establish one marker profile for every patient or every time point.

before: Measure, then infer: the measured features are fragment length, end sequences, genomic positions and chemical marks. A reference or trained model then turns them into a source estimate or a score, so the output is an inference and not a cell census, and no single fragment carries a cancer address. Tumour fragments are shorter on average, but most short fragments in a sample still come from normal cells because normal DNA outnumbers tumour DNA when the tumour fraction is low. These features can complement mutation tracking when few informative mutations are sampled, and neither a source estimate nor a score by itself establishes tumour location, stage, a resistance mechanism or benefit from acting on a result.

Evidence read: selecting fragments of 90 to 150 base pairs gave more than twofold median enrichment of tumour DNA in over 95% of cases among 344 plasma samples from 200 people with cancer (Mouliere 2018). A genome-wide fragmentation classifier detected 57% to more than 99% of seven cancer types at 98% specificity (area under the curve 0.94) in 236 patients and 245 healthy people, and located tissue of origin to a limited number of sites in 75% of cases (Cristiano 2019). Nucleosome footprints in cfDNA correlate with cell-type epigenetics (Snyder 2016). Each is a proof of principle in defined cohorts and does not transfer to another population, collection protocol or assay version.

Handling is part of the measurement: neither collection tube nor plasma processing time changed cfDNA fragment sizes in one study, but both could change genome-wide fragmentation patterns and fragment-end sequences, and a size profile that looks fine is an incomplete quality check (van der Pol 2022). In a fictional case a classifier trained on promptly processed plasma gives higher scores on samples transported under another protocol while DNA yield meets the minimum, and that does not show more cancer-associated DNA until the new conditions are validated.

The association between fragment patterns and nucleosome organisation provides information for inference, rather than a unique address stamped on each fragment. Fragment length is reported in base pairs, end patterns as defined proportions or sequence features, and a classifier score in the scale of its model. DNA extraction and analysis use a finite plasma aliquot, and the amount recovered differs from the amount drawn. Collection-to-separation time, storage and timing relative to treatment belong with the specimen. Validation has to follow the measured feature: retain collection and processing dates, reference mixtures and process controls, batch checks, and the population, assay version and cut-off used to develop and evaluate the model. before: How the read works: DNA methylation adds chemical marks to DNA bases without changing sequence, and many assays examine methylated cytosines next to guanines (CpG sites), using chemical or enzymatic conversion or other technologies. Normal cell types carry their own methylation patterns, so a mark is not a cancer label. Deconvolution estimates how much each reference cell type contributes to a mixture: a methylation atlas of 25 tissues and cell types attributed healthy-donor plasma cfDNA to white blood cells (55%), erythrocyte progenitors (30%), vascular endothelial cells (10%) and hepatocytes (1%), and its contributions also matched sepsis and islet transplantation (Moss 2018).

Scope: a classifier assigns a score or category and a deconvolution assigns source fractions, and both depend on the reference set, the model and the cut-off. Because tissue injury also adds normal DNA from an organ, an inferred organ contribution alone is not proof of cancer. A model validated in one population, collection protocol and assay version does not transfer automatically, and a score is not necessarily a calibrated probability.

before: The name has three expansions: minimal residual disease (small remaining amounts), measurable residual disease (used in blood-cancer guidance, stressing what the method can detect) and molecular residual disease (tumour-associated molecular signals after treatment, mostly ctDNA in solid tumours). Check which one a paper means. Cell-frequency thresholds in leukaemia, molecular ratios and plasma detection rules are different quantities, and the European LeukemiaNet update on acute myeloid leukaemia sets disease-specific techniques, materials, time points and thresholds that are not transferable to a solid tumour (Heuser 2021).

Residual disease on a surgical specimen is a different measurement: residual cancer burden is a defined tissue endpoint and is not interchangeable with a blood MRD call. In a fictional study a postoperative plasma test is negative but surgery shows residual invasive cancer. Neither must be wrong, because pathology examined tissue at surgery and the plasma assay sought a qualifying signal in a later blood sample, so dates, specimen and assay limits need reconciling before the pair is read. MRD negative means a method found no qualifying signal in one specimen and not that no cancer cell remains anywhere.

A residual-disease signal can select a research group at higher observed recurrence risk without showing which treatment helps that group. Clinical utility asks whether a test-guided strategy improves a meaningful outcome against an appropriate alternative. Disappearance of a marker is a separate proposed surrogate: it needs validation against the outcome for that setting, rather than becoming proof of cure. These are interpretation distinctions in the FDA November 2024 drug-development guidance, not a universal rule to change treatment.

fields.before: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that method, not proof that every cancer cell is absent. In leukaemia and myeloma it is measured by flow cytometry or NGS of marrow (clonoSEQ); in solid tumours it means ctDNA after surgery, covered under MRD / molecular residual disease testing. MRD positivity predicts relapse, MRD-guided escalation (IMvigor011) and de-escalation (DYNAMIC) are proven concepts, and MRD is an accepted endpoint in myeloma trials (FDA ODAC 2024). Readers meet it in the Colorectal, Pancreatic, Bladder & urothelial, DLBCL and Multiple myeloma entries and in CIRCULATE-Japan.
fields.after: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. Blood-cancer studies can use cell-based or molecular measurements, while solid-tumour studies can look for tumour-associated features in plasma. The disease, specimen, technique, time point and threshold define the result. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that method, not proof that every cancer cell is absent. Associations with recurrence, benefit from a test-guided treatment strategy, and validation of a surrogate endpoint are separate questions; evidence for one setting does not establish the others.

before: In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

A worked limit: for multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 patient-specific structural variants on 4,500 amplifiable copies, the theoretical limit is 1 / (4,500 x variants), which is 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million, at 47 variants. The 4.7 parts per million detection rested on a single mutant molecule, and one sample not detected at 4,500 copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies (Santonja 2023). Whole-genome sequencing of cfDNA integrates thousands of mutations and reached tumour-fraction sensitivity as low as 10 to the minus 5 (Zviran 2020).

Medians from different cohorts, schedules and confirmation rules cannot rank assays, and an earlier signal does not show that acting on it extends life.

before: Design contract, from the FDA guidance of November 2024: a tumour-informed approach sequences the tumour and selects variants to follow. Both still meet the same finite plasma tube, background attribution and calling rules.

Same-sample comparison: in serial plasma from people with breast cancer, tumour-informed assays showed the highest sensitivity at low ctDNA levels, with hybrid-capture sequencing of 1,347 to 7,491 tumour-identified mutations detecting an allele fraction of 2.4 parts per million and multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 structural variants reaching 4.7 parts per million (Santonja 2023). Each added tracked variant is another largely independent chance to catch a tumour fragment, and the theoretical limit 1 / (input copies x variants) falls as variants rise, but it applies to that assay and does not rank product categories.

Comparability, fictional: two studies report 90% and 75% detection, the first before treatment and the second after surgery. The higher percentage does not show the better assay, because disease burden, timing, case mix, missing samples and outcome definitions differ. A suitable comparison aligns these conditions, ideally on the same samples with prespecified rules. Labels such as tumour-naive, tumour-agnostic and tissue-free are method labels that need definition and do not establish that a test detects every cancer.

These are design considerations rather than a general ranking of sensitivity or clinical benefit.

before: Denominators, fictional arithmetic: a run records 12,000 events, and after excluding debris, cell pairs and dead-cell events 10,000 recovered gated cells remain, of which 1,000 are T-cell events and 100 bind a reagent. Binding is 100 / 1,000 = 10% of the T-cell parent, 100 / 10,000 = 1% of recovered cells and 100 / 12,000 = 0.83% of recorded events. All three are correct for their own question and exchanging them changes the claim. Nested gates show membership and not area, no cells per millilitre or whole-body total follows, and binding or marker identity does not show killing.

Method card, what it measures: light scatter and fluorescence from individual events in a prepared cell suspension, grouped by a chosen panel of stains. Input: whole blood, isolated cells or dissociated tissue, where preparation and staining use a defined aliquot and compatibility with later assays depends on fixation and other processing and tissue dissociation removes geography and can recover cell types unevenly. Output: event counts, percent of a named parent population, fluorescence in instrument-dependent units, and cells per volume only with a validated counting method. Controls: instrument checks, unstained and single-stain controls, viability, biological controls and fluorescence-minus-one controls for hard boundaries. Failure modes: dead cells, aggregates, weak markers, nonspecific staining, signal overlap, cell loss and inconsistent gates. It cannot tell unmeasured proteins, original tissue position, antigen specificity from general markers or benefit.

What compensation does and does not do: in multicolour analysis spectral overlap between detectors needs compensation, and a mathematical and experimental analysis showed that photon-counting statistics add a nonlinear error to compensated parameters while measurement and log-scale binning errors add linear ones, most visibly with red and far-red fluorochromes where less light is emitted (Roederer 2001). Compensation or spectral unmixing therefore corrects overlap and does not repair a poorly chosen stain or set a positivity gate. The community guidelines (Cossarizza 2021) are methods guidance on preparation, panels and analysis and give no universal immune-response cut-off. A degranulation marker on the cell surface is an activity readout that accompanied cytolysis in antigen-specific CD8 T cells and is not itself measured target-cell death (Betts 2003).

Gating is selection within recorded data, not physical collection. A typical analysis checks acquisition quality, excludes debris and cell pairs, assesses viability where the assay requires it, and identifies populations with a stated marker panel. Intracellular assays may assess viability before fixation; not every flow experiment studies living cells. Fluorescence-minus-one controls omit one stain while retaining the others and can help place a boundary, but do not establish antibody specificity. Tight earlier gates can discard unexpected or rare populations. Automated clusters still need biological and technical checks (Cossarizza 2021). A cell sorter can physically collect selected events for downstream work, subject to recovery, purity and functional-viability requirements; an analytical gate alone does not do this (Cossarizza 2019).

Absolute counts need a documented counting method, such as a suitable counting-bead standard or an instrument with validated absolute-count capability, with specimen volume and dilution retained. before: Method card, what it measures: the quantity an assay states, either a count of tumour-attributed molecules per volume of plasma (a concentration), a share of a named total (a fraction), or a call. How: sequencing or PCR on one finite plasma aliquot, then a calculation the laboratory defines. Keep the unit, the denominator and the assay version attached to every value.

Table, MTM/mL: mean tumour molecules per millilitre of plasma under the assay's own calculation across its tracked features. Boundary: a concentration estimated from tracked features, not the number of cancer cells per millilitre and not a share of anything.

Table, PPM: parts per million, a fraction multiplied by one million, so 1 PPM is 0.0001% and 100 PPM is 0.01%. Boundary: name the fraction being scaled, because 100 PPM of variant alleles, of evaluated DNA and of tumour-attributed molecules are three different claims.

Table, variant allele fraction: the share of evaluated alleles at one position that carry a stated variant. Boundary: it depends on copy number, on which clones carry the variant and on the measurement, and a variant present in a blood-cell clone counts the same way as one from a tumour.

before: Method card, what it measures: the difference between two prespecified event dates after the assay's qualifying rule, in days or months, with the number of evaluable people, the distribution and its uncertainty. Fictional arithmetic: six people recur at month 12 and are drawn every 2 months. A to D have first positives giving gaps of 2, 4, 6 and 8 months. E and F have no earlier positive. before: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

A worked example: in a multiplex PCR assay with a theoretical limit of 1 / (4,500 copies x variants), one sample not detected with 4,500 amplifiable copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies, and the authors note that detection at the theoretical limit rests on a single mutant molecule and is subject to the stochastic nature of sampling (Santonja 2023). A nominal detection limit from high-input validation material may not apply to a low-input clinical sample, so a laboratory with a 95% detection claim at 30 units of input cannot attach the same claim to a sample with 5 units without supporting data.

Analytical detection and clinical sensitivity answer different questions. FDA diagnostic-test guidance dated March 2007 defines clinical sensitivity by the proportion testing positive among people who have the specified condition, judged against the reference standard in the intended-use population. In a residual-disease study, disease definition, follow-up, draw schedule, evaluable samples and recurrence sites shape that denominator. An analytical limit measured in prepared material does not supply that clinical proportion, and a negative test does not establish absence of cancer.

Following a blood test from body to result separates biological availability, inclusion in the evaluated aliquot, recovery through processing, and the final calling rule. Low shedding, handling losses, background or a failed quality criterion can interrupt different steps. Repeated draws observe different times, but tumour biology and handling can make their errors correlated; they are not automatically independent repeats. A failed sample or an unbuildable reference needs its stated failure disposition rather than being silently called negative.

before: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

Fictional arithmetic: wells with 100,000 input cells give 30 spots after peptide stimulation and 5 spots with vehicle. Background-subtracted, that is 30 minus 5 = 25 spots per 100,000 cells, or 250 spot-forming units per million input cells. This is an arithmetic summary and not a positivity cut-off, replicates, positive controls and a prespecified response rule still apply, and in mixed PBMCs it is not the frequency of a particular T-cell subset. If the cells came from an expanded culture, the number describes the cultured cells and not the responding fraction of the original blood draw.

What the evidence does and does not support: the interferon gamma ELISpot is described as measuring the difference in the number of cells secreting the molecule with and without peptide, and interferon gamma is produced predominantly by natural killer and natural killer T cells as well as Th1 CD4 and CD8 effector T cells, so a mixed-cell spot does not by itself name the responding cell (Wykes and Renia protocol). In HIV vaccine research robust ELISpot responses were induced in a phase IIb trial that lacked efficacy, which challenged the assay's predictive power (Streeck 2009), and a validation in cynomolgus monkeys for responses to viral vector antigens (Yang 2022) validates that preparation and species and not cancer efficacy. Peptide added to cells can bypass the tumour's own processing and presentation, so a peptide response needs a separate bridge to natural tumour recognition.

Receptor sequencing asks which receptor sequences are represented and in what relative abundance. ELISpot asks how many input cells release the chosen molecule under the stated stimulation. An expanded sequence does not establish that it caused a spot, and a spot in mixed cells does not identify a receptor sequence. Connecting identity to recognition or killing requires additional experiments with suitable controls.

before: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. before: Source classes: cfDNA is DNA outside intact cells in a sample, and ctDNA is the tumour-derived part of that pool, so the two are related materials and not rival tests. The target-allele probability is not automatically a tumour-DNA fraction: copy number, variant multiplicity and clone representation matter.

Yield is not origin: in a fictional experiment equal 1 mL plasma aliquots give 2 and 4 nanograms of cfDNA and no tumour-attributed signal is reported. before: Leading programmes: Ebert (Dana-Farber/Broad) and Jaiswal (Stanford) who defined CHIP; Levine and Bolton (MSK) on therapy-related clonal haematopoiesis.

Clonal haematopoiesis (CH) is the broader phenomenon of blood-cell clones carrying acquired changes. In the 2022 WHO myeloid classification, CHIP requires a somatic mutation in a myeloid-malignancy-associated gene at a variant allele fraction of at least 2%, or at least 4% for X-linked gene mutations in males, without a diagnosed haematological disorder or unexplained cytopenia (Khoury 2022). Persistent unexplained cytopenia changes the classification question. These are criteria for a named category, not a rule that every smaller blood-cell clone is absent, tumour-derived or a sequencing error.

Which genes: in blood-cell exomes from 17,182 people most clonal variants fell in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, were rare before age 40, and were seen in 9.5% of people aged 70 to 79 (Jaiswal 2014). ASXL1 mutations were enriched in current or former smokers, and radiation, platinum and topoisomerase II inhibitors selected for DNA-damage-response genes (TP53, PPM1D, CHEK2), with sequential samples showing those clones outgrowing others after exposure (Bolton 2020). In 8,810 people with non-haematological cancers, PPM1D and TP53 mutations were associated with prior chemotherapy, and clonal haematopoiesis was found in 25% (Coombs 2017).

Source attribution in plasma, interpretation rule: TP53 is a tumour gene and also a therapy-selected blood-cell gene, so a TP53 variant in plasma after chemotherapy can come from either compartment. Matched white-blood-cell DNA and the tumour's variant list, where available, help assess its origin; some variants remain ambiguous. In Razavi's paired sequencing 53.2% of cfDNA mutations in 124 people with metastatic cancer and 81.6% in 47 controls without cancer had features of clonal haematopoiesis, and variants that could not be separated from white-blood-cell DNA kept an explicit ambiguous category, so subtracting every blood match is not a complete attribution method.

Fictional example: a plasma assay detects a variant that sensitive matched blood-cell sequencing finds at 0.8% VAF. The blood result supports a blood-cell contribution even below the 2% cut-off, but it does not make the variant CHIP or exclude a tumour contribution, because tumour evidence, shared variants and each method's limits still apply. Matched sequencing has its own gene coverage, depth and detection rules, so a clone below its sensitivity can stay unseen, and a clone finding is not a leukaemia diagnosis or a solid-tumour treatment instruction.

Reading the figures: a variant allele fraction counts variant alleles among the alleles evaluated and is not automatically the percentage of cells. Acquired (somatic) means not inherited and does not mean malignant. There is no age at which a plasma variant can simply be dismissed. Sequential samples show clones with DNA-damage-response mutations outgrowing others after radiation, platinum or topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure (Bolton 2020), which is selection of clones that can already be present and does not mean every new detection was caused by treatment.

before: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. One established epithelial method captures with EpCAM, then checks cell shape, a nucleus, cytokeratin and absence of CD45, which is one operational definition and not a universal rule for all circulating tumour cells or tumour types. Physical methods select by size or deformability and remove or retain different cells, so marker independence is not unbiased recovery. A negative capture, such as zero qualifying cells in 7.5 mL, does not show that no tumour cells circulate and does not predict a ctDNA result, because free DNA fragments are a separate analyte.

Scale and scope: in the CellSearch system, 1 of 344 healthy or non-malignant-disease subjects (0.3%) had two or more cells per 7.5 mL, against 36% of 2,183 samples from 964 people with metastatic carcinoma, with detection of two or more cells in 57% of prostate, 37% of breast, 30% of colorectal and 20% of lung cancer samples (Allard 2004). Spiked-cell recovery averaged at least 85% over 5 to 1,142 cells. These describe that device and population.

Prognosis is not utility: in a prospective study of 177 people with metastatic breast cancer, a baseline count of 5 or more per 7.5 mL in the training set went with a median progression-free survival of 2.7 months against 7.0 (Cristofanilli 2004). In SWOG S0500, of 595 evaluable patients 123 with persistently raised counts were randomised to continue or change chemotherapy, and median overall survival was 10.7 and 12.5 months (P = .98), so that early-switch strategy did not extend survival (Smerage 2014). That bounds one strategy and neither validates nor excludes other uses of the count.

Yu and colleagues reported epithelial and mesenchymal changes in circulating breast tumour cells and associations with progression (2013). As a measurement inference, enrichment requiring an epithelial marker can under-represent cells with little of that marker; physical capture has different selection effects. Neither route is a census of all circulating tumour cells. The study does not establish one marker profile for every patient or every time point.

before: Measure, then infer: the measured features are fragment length, end sequences, genomic positions and chemical marks. A reference or trained model then turns them into a source estimate or a score, so the output is an inference and not a cell census, and no single fragment carries a cancer address. Tumour fragments are shorter on average, but most short fragments in a sample still come from normal cells because normal DNA outnumbers tumour DNA when the tumour fraction is low. These features can complement mutation tracking when few informative mutations are sampled, and neither a source estimate nor a score by itself establishes tumour location, stage, a resistance mechanism or benefit from acting on a result.

Evidence read: selecting fragments of 90 to 150 base pairs gave more than twofold median enrichment of tumour DNA in over 95% of cases among 344 plasma samples from 200 people with cancer (Mouliere 2018). A genome-wide fragmentation classifier detected 57% to more than 99% of seven cancer types at 98% specificity (area under the curve 0.94) in 236 patients and 245 healthy people, and located tissue of origin to a limited number of sites in 75% of cases (Cristiano 2019). Nucleosome footprints in cfDNA correlate with cell-type epigenetics (Snyder 2016). Each is a proof of principle in defined cohorts and does not transfer to another population, collection protocol or assay version.

Handling is part of the measurement: neither collection tube nor plasma processing time changed cfDNA fragment sizes in one study, but both could change genome-wide fragmentation patterns and fragment-end sequences, and a size profile that looks fine is an incomplete quality check (van der Pol 2022). summary.before: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. A negative result means no qualifying signal was detected under that method, not proof that every cancer cell is absent. In leukaemia and myeloma it is measured by flow cytometry or NGS of marrow (clonoSEQ); in solid tumours it means ctDNA after surgery, covered under MRD / molecular residual disease testing. MRD positivity predicts relapse, MRD-guided escalation (IMvigor011) and de-escalation (DYNAMIC) are proven concepts, and MRD is an accepted endpoint in myeloma trials (FDA ODAC 2024). Readers meet it in the Colorectal, Pancreatic, Bladder & urothelial, DLBCL and Multiple myeloma entries and in CIRCULATE-Japan.
summary.after: Minimal, measurable and molecular residual disease (MRD) are related terms for small amounts of disease assessed after treatment with a specified method and specimen. Blood-cancer studies can use cell-based or molecular measurements, while solid-tumour studies can look for tumour-associated features in plasma. Associations with recurrence, benefit from a test-guided treatment strategy, and validation of a surrogate endpoint are separate questions; evidence for one setting does not establish the others.

before: The name has three expansions: minimal residual disease (small remaining amounts), measurable residual disease (used in blood-cancer guidance, stressing what the method can detect) and molecular residual disease (tumour-associated molecular signals after treatment, mostly ctDNA in solid tumours). Cell-frequency thresholds in leukaemia, molecular ratios and plasma detection rules are different quantities, and the European LeukemiaNet update on acute myeloid leukaemia sets disease-specific techniques, materials, time points and thresholds that are not transferable to a solid tumour (Heuser 2021).

Residual disease on a surgical specimen is a different measurement: residual cancer burden is a defined tissue endpoint and is not interchangeable with a blood MRD call. In a fictional study a postoperative plasma test is negative but surgery shows residual invasive cancer. Neither must be wrong, because pathology examined tissue at surgery and the plasma assay sought a qualifying signal in a later blood sample, so dates, specimen and assay limits need reconciling before the pair is read. MRD negative means a method found no qualifying signal in one specimen and not that no cancer cell remains anywhere.

A residual-disease signal can select a research group at higher observed recurrence risk without showing which treatment helps that group. Clinical utility asks whether a test-guided strategy improves a meaningful outcome against an appropriate alternative. Disappearance of a marker is a separate proposed surrogate: it needs validation against the outcome for that setting, rather than becoming proof of cure. These are interpretation distinctions in the FDA November 2024 drug-development guidance, not a universal rule to change treatment.

before: In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

A worked limit: for multiplex PCR across 21 to 47 patient-specific structural variants on 4,500 amplifiable copies, the theoretical limit is 1 / (4,500 x variants), which is 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million, at 47 variants. The 4.7 parts per million detection rested on a single mutant molecule, and one sample not detected at 4,500 copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies (Santonja 2023). Whole-genome sequencing of cfDNA integrates thousands of mutations and reached tumour-fraction sensitivity as low as 10 to the minus 5 (Zviran 2020).

Distant extracranial relapse was detected in 22 of 23 patients and brain-only relapse in 1 of 6. Medians from different cohorts, schedules and confirmation rules cannot rank assays, and an earlier signal does not show that acting on it extends life.

before: Design contract, from the FDA guidance of November 2024: a tumour-informed approach sequences the tumour and selects variants to follow. Comparability, fictional: two studies report 90% and 75% detection, the first before treatment and the second after surgery. The higher percentage does not show the better assay, because disease burden, timing, case mix, missing samples and outcome definitions differ. A suitable comparison aligns these conditions, ideally on the same samples with prespecified rules. These are design considerations rather than a general ranking of sensitivity or clinical benefit.

before: Denominators, fictional arithmetic: a run records 12,000 events, and after excluding debris, cell pairs and dead-cell events 10,000 recovered gated cells remain, of which 1,000 are T-cell events and 100 bind a reagent. All three are correct for their own question and exchanging them changes the claim. Nested gates show membership and not area, no cells per millilitre or whole-body total follows, and binding or marker identity does not show killing.

Method card, what it measures: light scatter and fluorescence from individual events in a prepared cell suspension, grouped by a chosen panel of stains. Input: whole blood, isolated cells or dissociated tissue, where preparation and staining use a defined aliquot and compatibility with later assays depends on fixation and other processing and tissue dissociation removes geography and can recover cell types unevenly. Output: event counts, percent of a named parent population, fluorescence in instrument-dependent units, and cells per volume only with a validated counting method. Controls: instrument checks, unstained and single-stain controls, viability, biological controls and fluorescence-minus-one controls for hard boundaries. Failure modes: dead cells, aggregates, weak markers, nonspecific staining, signal overlap, cell loss and inconsistent gates. It cannot tell unmeasured proteins, original tissue position, antigen specificity from general markers or benefit.

What compensation does and does not do: in multicolour analysis spectral overlap between detectors needs compensation, and a mathematical and experimental analysis showed that photon-counting statistics add a nonlinear error to compensated parameters while measurement and log-scale binning errors add linear ones, most visibly with red and far-red fluorochromes where less light is emitted (Roederer 2001). Compensation or spectral unmixing therefore corrects overlap and does not repair a poorly chosen stain or set a positivity gate. The community guidelines (Cossarizza 2021) are methods guidance on preparation, panels and analysis and give no universal immune-response cut-off. A degranulation marker on the cell surface is an activity readout that accompanied cytolysis in antigen-specific CD8 T cells and is not itself measured target-cell death (Betts 2003).

Gating is selection within recorded data, not physical collection. A typical analysis checks acquisition quality, excludes debris and cell pairs, assesses viability where the assay requires it, and identifies populations with a stated marker panel. Intracellular assays may assess viability before fixation; not every flow experiment studies living cells. Fluorescence-minus-one controls omit one stain while retaining the others and can help place a boundary, but do not establish antibody specificity. Tight earlier gates can discard unexpected or rare populations. Automated clusters still need biological and technical checks (Cossarizza 2021). A cell sorter can physically collect selected events for downstream work, subject to recovery, purity and functional-viability requirements; an analytical gate alone does not do this (Cossarizza 2019).

Absolute counts need a documented counting method, such as a suitable counting-bead standard or an instrument with validated absolute-count capability, with specimen volume and dilution retained. before: For independent random target-molecule counts with Poisson mean lambda, the chance of none is exp(-lambda). At lambda = 1 this is 36.8%, so an average of one does not guarantee a molecule. In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

A worked example: in a multiplex PCR assay with a theoretical limit of 1 / (4,500 copies x variants), one sample not detected with 4,500 amplifiable copies was detected at 7.9 parts per million when re-assayed with 27,000 copies, and the authors note that detection at the theoretical limit rests on a single mutant molecule and is subject to the stochastic nature of sampling (Santonja 2023). A nominal detection limit from high-input validation material may not apply to a low-input clinical sample, so a laboratory with a 95% detection claim at 30 units of input cannot attach the same claim to a sample with 5 units without supporting data.

Analytical detection and clinical sensitivity answer different questions. FDA diagnostic-test guidance dated March 2007 defines clinical sensitivity by the proportion testing positive among people who have the specified condition, judged against the reference standard in the intended-use population. In a residual-disease study, disease definition, follow-up, draw schedule, evaluable samples and recurrence sites shape that denominator. An analytical limit measured in prepared material does not supply that clinical proportion, and a negative test does not establish absence of cancer.

Following a blood test from body to result separates biological availability, inclusion in the evaluated aliquot, recovery through processing, and the final calling rule. Low shedding, handling losses, background or a failed quality criterion can interrupt different steps. Repeated draws observe different times, but tumour biology and handling can make their errors correlated; they are not automatically independent repeats. A failed sample or an unbuildable reference needs its stated failure disposition rather than being silently called negative.

before: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

Fictional arithmetic: wells with 100,000 input cells give 30 spots after peptide stimulation and 5 spots with vehicle. Background-subtracted, that is 30 minus 5 = 25 spots per 100,000 cells, or 250 spot-forming units per million input cells. This is an arithmetic summary and not a positivity cut-off, replicates, positive controls and a prespecified response rule still apply, and in mixed PBMCs it is not the frequency of a particular T-cell subset. If the cells came from an expanded culture, the number describes the cultured cells and not the responding fraction of the original blood draw.

What the evidence does and does not support: the interferon gamma ELISpot is described as measuring the difference in the number of cells secreting the molecule with and without peptide, and interferon gamma is produced predominantly by natural killer and natural killer T cells as well as Th1 CD4 and CD8 effector T cells, so a mixed-cell spot does not by itself name the responding cell (Wykes and Renia protocol). In HIV vaccine research robust ELISpot responses were induced in a phase IIb trial that lacked efficacy, which challenged the assay's predictive power (Streeck 2009), and a validation in cynomolgus monkeys for responses to viral vector antigens (Yang 2022) validates that preparation and species and not cancer efficacy. Peptide added to cells can bypass the tumour's own processing and presentation, so a peptide response needs a separate bridge to natural tumour recognition.

Receptor sequencing asks which receptor sequences are represented and in what relative abundance. ELISpot asks how many input cells release the chosen molecule under the stated stimulation. An expanded sequence does not establish that it caused a spot, and a spot in mixed cells does not identify a receptor sequence. Connecting identity to recognition or killing requires additional experiments with suitable controls.

before: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

Handling is evidence: in HIV vaccine assay studies, the time from venipuncture to cryopreservation was the most important parameter, and blood processed at 24 hours compared with within 8 hours lost on average about 8% of PBMC viability, about 32% of cell recovery and 36% to 56% of interferon gamma T-cell frequencies by ELISpot, which led the authors to recommend cryopreservation within 8 hours (Bull 2007). That is a finding for those protocols and assays and is not a universal schedule for cancer assays. A rapidly processed baseline and a delayed follow-up can therefore confound a biological comparison, and a high viability percentage alone does not show that every population or function was preserved.

Controls are collection and processing timestamps, anticoagulant, storage, counting and viability methods and matched handling across time points. before: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.

Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.

Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

before: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Binding is 100 / 1,000 = 10% of the T-cell parent, 100 / 10,000 = 1% of recovered cells and 100 / 12,000 = 0.83% of recorded events. All three are correct for their own question and exchanging them changes the claim. Nested gates show membership and not area, no cells per millilitre or whole-body total follows, and binding or marker identity does not show killing.

Method card, what it measures: light scatter and fluorescence from individual events in a prepared cell suspension, grouped by a chosen panel of stains. Input: whole blood, isolated cells or dissociated tissue, where preparation and staining use a defined aliquot and compatibility with later assays depends on fixation and other processing and tissue dissociation removes geography and can recover cell types unevenly. Output: event counts, percent of a named parent population, fluorescence in instrument-dependent units, and cells per volume only with a validated counting method. Controls: instrument checks, unstained and single-stain controls, viability, biological controls and fluorescence-minus-one controls for hard boundaries. Failure modes: dead cells, aggregates, weak markers, nonspecific staining, signal overlap, cell loss and inconsistent gates. It cannot tell unmeasured proteins, original tissue position, antigen specificity from general markers or benefit.

What compensation does and does not do: in multicolour analysis spectral overlap between detectors needs compensation, and a mathematical and experimental analysis showed that photon-counting statistics add a nonlinear error to compensated parameters while measurement and log-scale binning errors add linear ones, most visibly with red and far-red fluorochromes where less light is emitted (Roederer 2001). Compensation or spectral unmixing therefore corrects overlap and does not repair a poorly chosen stain or set a positivity gate. The community guidelines (Cossarizza 2021) are methods guidance on preparation, panels and analysis and give no universal immune-response cut-off. A degranulation marker on the cell surface is an activity readout that accompanied cytolysis in antigen-specific CD8 T cells and is not itself measured target-cell death (Betts 2003).

Gating is selection within recorded data, not physical collection. A typical analysis checks acquisition quality, excludes debris and cell pairs, assesses viability where the assay requires it, and identifies populations with a stated marker panel. Intracellular assays may assess viability before fixation; not every flow experiment studies living cells. Fluorescence-minus-one controls omit one stain while retaining the others and can help place a boundary, but do not establish antibody specificity. Tight earlier gates can discard unexpected or rare populations. Automated clusters still need biological and technical checks (Cossarizza 2021). A cell sorter can physically collect selected events for downstream work, subject to recovery, purity and functional-viability requirements; an analytical gate alone does not do this (Cossarizza 2019).

Absolute counts need a documented counting method, such as a suitable counting-bead standard or an instrument with validated absolute-count capability, with specimen volume and dilution retained. Counts of recorded events, percentages of a gate and cells per original blood volume are different outputs. The 2021 community guidelines describe both bead-based and instrument-based counting in specific protocols; neither makes every marker panel a validated clinical test.
